message.content:
1. (HIGH) — global
   Finding: OEM cost target violated by 24 % (brief caps at £1,800; report shows £2,234 OEM transfer price).
   Evidence: “£1,800 max OEM cost” in brief; cost stack page 1: “= OEM transfer price £2,234.27”.
   Root cause in chain: Engine B (price estimates) + G2 cost-reality gate never received the brief’s hard cap as a hard constraint; no cross-check against brief financial targets.
   Fix recommendation: Add brief financial targets to G0 physics ledger (class-floors.ts) and make G2 reject any BoM whose OEM transfer price exceeds the cap.

2. (HIGH) — SECTION 1 · BRIEF & REQUIREMENTS
   Finding: Envelope payload limit (1,500 kg) is physically impossible for a 90 kg residential unit and contradicts the stated gross mass.
   Evidence: “Envelope payload limit 1,500 kg max payload”; “Maximum gross mass 90 kg”.
   Root cause in chain: structure_containment.derived_parameters generator (Gemini 3.1 Pro) hallucinated pallet specs without scale check; G0.5 brief-target-reconciliation only compared kW, not mass.
   Fix recommendation: Extend G0.5 to also reconcile mass and envelope parameters against class-floors.ts residential heat-pump bounds.

3. (HIGH) — SECTION 6 · BILL OF MATERIALS
   Finding: Multiple major structural parts priced at £7.81 despite being large custom-fabricated galvanized steel assemblies.
   Evidence: “Galvanized Steel Frame custom fab HP-UK-FR-90 ~ £7.81 Est. < .5x”; same price repeated for outer shell, base plate, compressor shroud, etc.
   Root cause in chain: Engine B price-estimate fallback used a single “structural metal” curve with 0.080 multiplier regardless of part size; no geometry-aware costing.
   Fix recommendation: Replace Engine B flat multiplier with a simple area/volume-based estimator (or call a lightweight CAD cost model) before writing line prices.

4. (HIGH) — SECTION 2 · REGULATORY & COMPLIANCE
   Finding: Mandatory EMC 2014/30/EU standard omitted from declared compliance list despite inverter-driven compressor.
   Evidence: Compliance gate WARN: “1 mandatory standard not declared … EMC 2014/30/EU”; table lists only EU 517/2014, PED, MD, etc.
   Root cause in chain: G1b compliance gate (class-standards.ts) only checks standards explicitly mentioned in the brief; brief never listed EMC.
   Fix recommendation: Make G1b also inject all class-mandatory standards for the detected jurisdiction (UK/EU) regardless of brief text.

5. (MED) — global
   Finding: 67 fabricated or unverifiable part numbers remain in the final BoM after G5 verification.
   Evidence: Appendix A: “Stripped (fakes): 67”; “67 part numbers could not be verified against DigiKey / Mouser / Farnell”.
   Root cause in chain: Generator (Gemini 3.1 Pro) + R1/R2/R3/R4 synthesis stages freely invented plausible-looking SKUs; G5 only post-filters instead of constraining generation.
   Fix recommendation: Add a deterministic part-number whitelist / regex validator inside the Generator stage (or at R1–R4) keyed to known manufacturer catalogues before any line is emitted.

6. (HIGH) — SECTION 0 · OPERATIONAL HEADLINE
   Finding: Design thermal output and SCOP are simply copied from the brief without any physics-led sanity check against the chosen components.
   Evidence: “Design thermal output 8 kW”; “Seasonal coefficient of performance 3.50 SCOP”; assumptions say “From brief target performance”.
   Root cause in chain: G0 physics ledger only stores class floors; no forward simulation pass that recomputes SCOP from compressor, coil, and fan selections.
   Fix recommendation: Insert a lightweight steady-state cycle model (or at minimum a COP look-up table) after Module 4 synthesis and feed result back into G0.5 reconciliation.
